groups.label: Cabinet test inputs, Gottlieb-numbered switch matrix, and synthetic flipper column
groups.notes:
#### Matrix conversion

`MACHINE_DRIVER_START(gts3)` in `src/wpc/gts3.c` registers `MDRV_SWITCH_CONV(gts3_sw2m, gts3_m2sw)`, so public switch numbers are Gottlieb's own decimal notation: the tens digit is the strobe (matrix column) and the units digit the return (row).

| Function | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| `gts3_sw2m(no)` | `(no / 10 + 1) * 8 + no % 10`, or `-1` when `no % 10 > 7` |
| `gts3_m2sw(col, row)` | `row - 8` for internal column 0, otherwise `(col - 1) * 10 + row` |

A number whose last digit is 8 or 9 has no switch: `gts3_sw2m` returns `-1`, and `core_setSw`/`core_getSw` do not bounds-check the index they then use, so never write one.

#### Switch matrix

The CPU strobes up to twelve columns with the same 12-bit shift register that strobes the lamp matrix (`xvia_0_b_w`, `LDATA`/`LSTRB`), and reads the eight returns on VIA U4 port A through `xvia_0_a_r`, which returns `~core_getSwCol(GTS3locals.lampColumn)`. The public matrix is therefore `0-7`, `10-17`, ..., `110-117` (internal columns 1-12). The read is complemented in hardware, so public `1` is the closed-contact reading the CPU sees. No `INITGAME*` macro in `src/wpc/gts3games.c` sets an inverted-switch mask, so PinMAME normalizes nothing per game: a switch the ROM treats as active at public `1` has a contact that rests open.

With PinMAME keyboard handling on, `SWITCH_UPDATE(GTS3)` also rewrites the low bits of internal column 1 (public `0-7`) from the cabinet port, and the port layout follows the game's `INITGAME*` macro (`src/wpc/gts3.h`):

| Macro | Port flag | Public addresses rewritten |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `INITGAME2` (`GTS32_COMPORTS`) | `0x8000` | `0` Coin 2, `1` Coin 1, `2` Coin 3, `3` Coin 4, `4` Start, `5` Tournament (toggle), `6` Coin Door (toggle) |
| `INITGAME1` (`GTS31_COMPORTS`) and `INITGAME_IC` (`GTS3_IC_COMPORTS`) | `0x4000` | `0` Coin 2, `1` Coin 1, `2` Coin 3, `3` Coin 4, `4` Start |
| `INITGAME` (`GTS3_COMPORTS`) | none | `0` Coin 2, `1` Coin 1, `2` Coin 3, `3` Start, `4` Left Advance, `5` Right Advance |

The port labels are emulator key names, not the game's switch names; take those from the game's own switch test. With keyboard handling off, every one of these addresses keeps what the host writes.

#### Cabinet test inputs

Internal column 0 is not part of the matrix. `SWITCH_UPDATE(GTS3)` reads four of its bits back through `core_getSw` into dedicated latches every update (`GTS3_SWDIAG`, `GTS3_SWTILT`, `GTS3_SWSLAM`, `GTS3_SWPRIN` in `src/wpc/gts3.h`):

| Address | Constant | CPU read path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-8` | `GTS3_SWDIAG` | Test (diagnostic) switch: VIA U4 `PB3` on the DMD generation and the second alpha generation, VIA U4 `CA1` on the first alpha generation |
| `-7` | `GTS3_SWTILT` | Tilt: VIA U4 `PB4` |
| `-6` | `GTS3_SWSLAM` | Slam tilt: VIA U4 `CA1` (on the first alpha generation `PB3`) |
| `-5` | `GTS3_SWPRIN` | Printer present: the communications adapter status `aux1_r` returns |

`dmd_u4_pb_r` and `alpha_u4_pb_r` copy the latches without inversion (the source comments say `NOT INVERTED!`). With keyboard handling on, the cabinet port rewrites them from the Diagnostic, Ball Tilt, Slam Tilt and Printer keys; with it off they keep the host's writes. Bits `-4` to `-1` are never read.

#### Flipper column

`core_updateSw` (`src/wpc/core.c`) keeps the cabinet flipper buttons in internal column 15 for `GEN_GTS3` (its `flipSwCol` test), not in `CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL`. `gts3_m2sw(15, row)` publishes that column at `140-147`:

| Address | Bit | Position |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `140` | `CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT` | Lower right end-of-stroke |
| `141` | `CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT` | Lower right button |
| `142` | `CORE_SWLLFLIPEOSBIT` | Lower left end-of-stroke |
| `143` | `CORE_SWLLFLIPBUTBIT` | Lower left button |
| `144` | `CORE_SWURFLIPEOSBIT` | Upper right end-of-stroke |
| `145` | `CORE_SWURFLIPBUTBIT` | Upper right button |
| `146` | `CORE_SWULFLIPEOSBIT` | Upper left end-of-stroke |
| `147` | `CORE_SWULFLIPBUTBIT` | Upper left button |

Every pinned System 3 driver declares its flippers with `FLIP_SWNO(l, r)` (two alpha games with `FLIP_SW(FLIP_L)`), never `FLIP_SOL`, `FLIP_EOS` or an upper `FLIP_SW`, so `locals.flipMask` holds only the two lower button bits. With keyboard handling off, `core_updateSw` reads `141` and `143` as the host wrote them, copies them into the game's `FLIP_SWNO` matrix switches on every update (overwriting any direct write there), and fabricates the synthetic flipper outputs `45-48` from them while the game-on relay (solenoid `32`) is energized. The ROM cannot read column 15: the 12-bit strobe reaches internal columns 1-12 only. The VPinMAME library `GTS3.VBS` names the same addresses `swLRFlip = 141`, `swLLFlip = 143`, `swURFlip = 145` and `swULFlip = 147`.

groups.label: Driver-board outputs, relays, and synthetic flipper outputs
groups.notes:
#### Physical outputs

`solenoid_w` (`src/wpc/gts3.c`, CPU writes to `0x2030-0x2033`) stores four bytes into `coreGlobals.pulsedSolState`, so bit `n-1` is public solenoid `n` for `1-32`. `GTS3_interface_update` copies that state into `coreGlobals.solenoids` every `GTS3_SOLSMOOTH` (4) video frames, so a pulse shorter than that window can be lost or stretched in the binary solenoid stream. A game's own Relay & Solenoid Test names each output, so take the pairing from that game's test rather than a sibling's: Stargate's displays the driver number counted from `0`, one less than the public address that fires.

`gts3dmd_init` and `GTS3_alpha_common_init` set the platform's relay conventions, which the games' tests corroborate by name:

| Public | Platform role |
| --- | --- |
| `26` | 'A' relay: lightbox insert (backbox) lamps |
| `31` | 'T' relay: playfield general illumination (the tilt relay) |
| `32` | 'Q' relay: game on; `GTS3_interface_update` passes its state to `core_updateSw` as the flipper enable |

`coreGlobals.nGI = 0`: there is no separate general-illumination channel, and the relays are ordinary solenoid outputs. The per-game `strncasecmp` blocks in the two init functions only choose PWM brightness models (`CORE_MODOUT_BULB_89_20V_DC_GTS3`, `CORE_MODOUT_LED`, ...) for flasher and LED outputs; they model brightness, not fitment.

#### Synthetic flipper outputs

No System 3 driver sets `FLIP_SOL`, so `core_updateSw` fabricates the lower flipper outputs from the flipper-column buttons `141`/`143` while `32` is energized. `core_getAllSol`, which feeds LibPinMAME's changed-solenoid reports outside physical-output mode, publishes `45`/`46` for the lower right button and `47`/`48` for the lower left one, both bits of a pair together. In physical-output (modulated) mode `vp_getChangedSolenoids` reads `physicOutputState` instead, which System 3 never writes above `32`. The upper-flipper range `33-36`, the `37-44` extension range and the simulator outputs `49-50` carry nothing on this platform.

groups.label: Gottlieb-numbered lamp matrix and auxiliary driver board outputs
groups.notes:
#### Lamp matrix

`MACHINE_DRIVER_START(gts3)` also registers `MDRV_LAMP_CONV(gts3_sw2m, gts3_m2sw)`, and `vp_getChangedLamps` reports internal lamp column `c` (0-based), row `r` as `gts3_m2sw(c + 1, r)`, that is `c * 10 + r`. Public lamp numbers are therefore Gottlieb's decimal lamp numbers and **start at `0`**: `0-7`, `10-17`, ..., `110-117`.

`xvia_0_b_w` shifts a 12-bit column strobe (two 74HC164s, the same strobe the switch matrix uses) and `lds_w` (`0x2040`) latches the eight row outputs, so the matrix is twelve columns by eight rows. The emulation accumulates a frame until the strobe restarts at the first column.

#### Auxiliary driver board

When a game declares `hw.lampCol > 4` (the last argument of its `INITGAME*` macro), `xvia_1_b_w` writes VIA U5 port B (`DX0-DX7`, connector A1P6) into `coreGlobals.lampMatrix[12]`, published at `120-127`. The source calls these "flashers driven by auxiliary board". Games with `hw.lampCol = 4` use the same port for an extra LED display or nothing, and publish nothing at `120-127`. `coreGlobals.nLamps = 64 + hw.lampCol * 8`, so a definition narrows this ceiling to its own game's declaration.

There is no general-illumination lamp channel: G.I. is switched by the 'T' and 'A' relays on the solenoid outputs.
